summary: This diff is purely additive (627 insertions, 0 deletions across 5 new/extended files) and touches only ai-os/ audit docs, MASTER_INDEX.yaml, and two shell scripts under scripts/ -- no migrations, schema, auth, permission, payment, billing, rls, or .env paths, and no .github/workflows/** changes, so the tier1 classification per SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md is correct. deploy-live-scripts.sh is well-built: it derives its copy set structurally from `git ls-files scripts/` rather than a hand-maintained exclude list (so operational-only live files like crontab backups, cost/credit scripts, and the OpenRouter proxy are provably never touched), backs up any live file it overwrites with a timestamped .bak before replacing it, never deletes, uses process substitution (`< <(...)`) so its DEPLOYED/UNCHANGED/FAILED counters correctly persist outside the loop, and reports a real, verifiable idempotent run (35 deployed / 17 unchanged / 0 failed, then 0 / 52 / 0 on immediate re-run). The two new YAML docs are honest and well-evidenced audit artifacts (real diff -q, grep -c, and hash-based verification cited throughout, including explicit caveats like the unread root crontab and 24 still-untracked core orchestration scripts) rather than self-reported claims. No injection, path-traversal, or credential-handling issues found in the shell scripts.
issues: Wiring deploy-live-scripts.sh into sync-repos.sh's 2-hourly cron means any future tier1-auto-merged PR touching scripts/ now propagates to live production scripts within 2 hours with no further human gate -- this is the intended fix, but it meaningfully raises the stakes of every future scripts/ tier1 review and should be kept in mind by subsequent Superboss audits.

sync-repos.sh calls deploy-live-scripts.sh unconditionally after its per-repo pull loop, even if the claude-control pull was SKIPPED (uncommitted local changes) or FAILED (non-fast-forward) -- it will still deploy whatever is currently checked out in that worktree as if authoritative. Low practical impact since the deploy step is content-diffed and idempotent, but tightening this to skip deploy when the claude-control pull itself did not succeed would be more correct.

The audit docs themselves flag that root/system crontab could not be read this session (no sudo password available), so the 'no other deploy mechanism exists' conclusion rests on user-level and filesystem-visible checks only -- already honestly caveated in the docs, not a code defect, but noting for visibility.
